ratings_why.fun: Copying the shop's best or your own carry and choosing when to cash in Worn is a rich draft, but many cards read as two texts at once, which slows every turn.
ratings_why.distinct: Earns 8 over 7 because Worn makes time a resource you choose to spend (let it run or Unmask for applause), and a Guise carries tribe, so a Changeling can become a Bird and Fly South; no tribe today plays like that.

verdict_why: The Glamourer and Seamstress chain can loop forever as written, and a Stock of the Lady under Wicker Moll is unreadable; both are small, real fixes.

points.text: Glamour-Veil Seamstress plus a unit Guised as Glamourer of the Knowe loops: each new Guise fires the copied When played, which gives another Guise, which Unmasks and feeds Knowe Usher. Add "Once a turn per unit" or say a copied When played can't give a Guise.
Under Wicker Moll a Stock of The Lady Under the Hill has her text, but it's unclear whether that Stock counts as a "copy of her". Say so in the Lady's or Moll's text.
"Guise X" (this wears X) and "give a unit the Guise of X" (Glamourer) are two phrasings of one verb. Use one form, such as "wear X's Guise", so a player never wonders who changes.
Most shop units' text is When played, which a Guise doesn't trigger, so Foundling often copies nothing useful. Let Foundling fire the copied When played once, so the first copy feels like something.
Pip Unlike asks the player to flip left, right, front and behind in their head. Have the card show the flipped text, so the mirror joke reads at a glance.

standouts.why: Penny Second takes your carry's place and sends the real one to the shop: the folklore of the turned-away duchess, done in one play.
Grandfer Acorn can't help giving himself away every turn, and that cuts against the Long Con build, so keeping him is a real choice.
Fetch of the Front Rank is the clearest card in the tribe: become the enemy across, and you can plan it from their last board.

weakest.why: Pip Unlike is charming, but mirror-flipped copied text is the hardest thing in the tribe to read.
Clerk of Exchanges is a plain swap with no hook of its own; it only shines next to Stocks or Bettie.
Wicker Prentice is a blank stat copy; the Stock fantasy only wakes up once Wicker Moll is down.

flags.note: Copied When played that gives a Guise can chain with no limit (see p1).
Whether a Stock of the Lady counts as a copy of her isn't stated.
Tam Twice turns every Guise into a triple piece; Discover chains could run away.
Bettie has no cap and fires often with Moll, the Prentice and the Assessor.
Mirror-backwards text needs the card to show the flipped words, or players misread it.
